cefrAlignment: Matches B1 (CEFR CV: can follow detailed directions and understand simple technical information such as directions in a building or town): short monologues and dialogues with high-frequency route language (second turning, straight over the roundabout, opposite, between).
examFidelity: Mirrors IELTS Part 2 map labelling (lettered plan, extra letters, places asked in audio order) and TOEIC Part 3/4 location questions; I checked every map answer against the SVG coordinates (pharmacy A, library C, bookshop E, supermarket F, Grand Hotel G; B, D, H unused; model answer H) and all are correct and unique.
fixes: Note completion: added 'carpark' as an accepted spelling of 'car park'.
Map alt text: made the positions of C and D precise (north-west and north-east corners of Mill Road and High Street; D opposite the Cinema) so the text matches the SVG exactly.
openConcerns: Practice audio 1 is about 170 words, slightly above the 60–150-word B1 guide, but it carries five map items and stays at B1 difficulty.
The museum talk uses US vocabulary (elevator, restrooms, second floor) while the lesson is otherwise UK English; this is intentional for TOEIC and the vocabulary list notes lift/elevator.
learnerOutcome: A learner who completes the lesson can follow spoken directions on a street plan, keep track of left and right after turning, and use landmarks and prepositions of place to locate buildings and take route notes.
